title: drain_timeout_secs as Option<u64> with serde default
description: Both reader [limits] and transit [peering] expose drain_timeout_secs as Option<u64> with #[serde(default)] rather than a required field or a type-level default function. This means: (1) existing config files that omit the field continue to parse without error, giving backward compatibility; (2) the code reads .unwrap_or(30) at the call site, making the effective default visible in the code rather than buried in a serde attribute; (3) the None state is meaningful — it can be logged or tested distinctly from an explicit zero, which would mean 'exit immediately'. Alternative rejected: a dedicated default_drain_timeout() function returning 30u64 used as #[serde(default = "default_drain_timeout")]. That hides the default in a small helper function and makes the field non-optional (u64 instead of Option<u64>), losing the ability to distinguish 'not set' from 'set to 30'.
